frase_gancho.texto: The language of the Mexica is still alive: in embroidery, painted paper and altars of corn.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: You arrive at the last hall, the hall of the Nahua Peoples. They are the most numerous Indigenous people of Mexico: more than a million and a half people speak Nahuatl, the language of the Mexica, and they live in very different regions, from the Huasteca to the mountains of Guerrero and the towns around the volcanoes. Many words you use every day, like chocolate, tomato or petate, come from their language. This hall brings together an embroidered huipil, a painting on Amate Paper and an altar of thanksgiving for the first ears of tender corn. Here the circle closes: the language of the stone gods you saw downstairs is still spoken today.
